U: › [ U ] a solid substance containing a lot of fat that becomes soft and melts when warm
› [ U ] the soft, yellowish substance inside your ears

T: › [ T ] to put a thin layer of wax on the surface of something, either to make it waterproof or to improve its appearance
› [ T ] to remove hair from someone's body by covering it in a thin layer of warm wax that is then pulled off

I: › [ I ] formal When the moon waxes, it gradually appears larger and rounder each day.

NONE: › to speak or write in the stated way
熱情洋溢／滔滔不絕地說（或寫）（等等）

example: She watched the wax as it dripped down the side of the candle.
她注視著蠟從蠟燭邊緣滴落下來。
I've waxed the floor so it's rather slippery.
我剛給地板打了蠟，所以恐怕會有點滑。
她對腿部做了熱蠟除毛。
My mother always used to wax lyrical about the lemon trees in her family's garden.
我母親過去總是會深情地談起她家中花園裡的那些檸檬樹。

NONE: › to grow stronger and then weaker again

example: His commitment to democracy and free markets has waxed and waned with his political fortunes.
他對民主和自由市場的熱情隨著他自己政治命運的起伏而時強時弱。
